invariance_note.mathematical_basis: On purely categorical records (no numeric vitals), Gower, Euclidean (one-hot), and Cosine (one-hot) are exact monotonic transformations of Hamming distance: D_cosine = D_gower = D_hamming / p, and D_euclid = sqrt(2 * D_hamming) = sqrt(2p * D_gower). Consequently, all evaluation protocols that depend strictly on the rank-order of distances (kNN classification, precision@k retrieval, and complete-linkage minimax clustering) produce mathematically identical rankings and scores across all three metrics. In contrast, methods that average, sum, or preserve metric ratios (average linkage, silhouette score, MDS) differ due to the non-linear square-root transform in Euclidean distance.
